clue.text: Cater differently, with undressed salad to start menu

indicators.note: to start puts the trimmed salad at the front of the answer
undressed means stripped of its outer covering, so salad loses its first and last letters
differently says the letters of cater are arranged another way

explanation.surface: A caterer is told to change things and open the menu with a salad that has no dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undressed' strips salad to ALA; 'differently' rearranges CATER into CARTE; 'to start' puts ALA first.
explanation.definitionFit: A la carte describes ordering separately priced dishes from a restaurant's full list, so the phrase stands for that kind of menu.

clue.text: Old Queen going round old lover's wing

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the queen's name encloses the former partner

parts.note: Anne was Queen of Great Britain in the early 1700s
an ex is a former partner; the 's means is, a link

explanation.surface: A former queen circles round her past lover's part of the palace.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extension added to a building, like a side wing.

clue.text: A rich person who's fashionable too!

parts.note: a swell is an old-fashioned word for a stylish, wealthy person

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a wealthy socialite is also stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in addition or also, exactly as the adverb does.

clue.text: A British range peaks in Italy

parts.note: the Pennines are a chain of hills running down northern England

explanation.surface: A British mountain chain has peaks located in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pennines are the hills forming the 'backbone of England'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain chain running the length of the Italian peninsula.

clue.text: Anyone for hard rock? I'm playing conservative circles

indicators.note: circles means surrounds, so the party member goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

indicators.note: playing means performing, so the letters of hard rock and I'm are put in a new order

parts.note: the letters of I'm without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A musician asks whether anyone wants heavy rock, while a Tory hangs around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anyone' sits at the front looking like part of the question; it is the definition, and the rest is a container with an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning any ordinary person at all, whoever they may be.

clue.text: Silly duffers start to frolic in peaceful places

indicators.note: to frolic means to romp about, so the letters skip around into a new order
start picks the first letter of duffers

explanation.surface: Clumsy fools begin to play about in tranquil spots.
explanation.walkthrough: SILLY plus D, the start of 'duffers', is rearranged by 'to frolic'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a scene or spot of pastoral calm and happiness, so the plural names tranquil settings.

clue.text: Prominent Celtic member was enough to secure game

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so did encloses the game

parts.note: did, as in that did, means sufficed
RU is the abbreviation for rugby union

explanation.surface: A star player at Celtic, the Glasgow football club, did enough to win a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celtic' suggests the Glasgow football club; it is the ancient priesthood. RU is rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: A druid was a priest and leader in ancient Celtic society, a senior figure of that order.

clue.text: How high leaders trade places, and how far from the 11

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters, and trade places means the first two swap

parts.note: altitude is height above a level

explanation.surface: Bosses swap roles and ask about heights and distances from the 11.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 refers to the answer at 11-across, the equator.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude measures angular distance north or south of the Earth's middle circle.

clue.text: Highly skilled guitarist is quiet and looking more embarrassed

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
embarrassment makes you go red, so more so is redder

explanation.surface: A virtuoso guitarist turns shy and blushes ever deeper.
explanation.walkthrough: Shredding is rock slang for fast, technically dazzling guitar playing.
explanation.definitionFit: In rock slang a shredder is a virtuoso who plays very fast, flashy lead guitar.

clue.text: They say you got into blessing cosmetic work

indicators.note: got into means entered, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: beatification is the Church declaring someone blessed

indicators.note: they say means the next word is heard rather than read

parts.note: you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: People say you've taken up a blessing in beauty treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: Beatification is the Catholic step before sainthood, declaring someone blessed; 'They say' means hear 'you' as a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Beautification is making something attractive, which is what cosmetic treatment aims to do.

clue.text: Education begins once more with this neologism

definitions.text: Education begins once more with this
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the start of a new school term, when lessons resume
second meaning: a newly coined word or expression

explanation.walkthrough: The first stretch describes the start of a school period; the second is a freshly minted expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is literally a freshly coined word, and a school year restarts with a fresh session of teaching.

clue.text: Torque converter includes a zero- degree line

indicators.note: includes means the letter a sits inside the rearranged letters
a converter changes one thing into another, so the letters of torque are reworked

explanation.surface: A torque converter, a car's transmission part, apparently contains a line at zero degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converter' rearranges TORQUE; 'includes' places A within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is measured from the circle round the Earth's middle, which sits at zero degrees.

clue.text: Polymer stored by foxy landlady

indicators.note: stored by says the answer is kept inside the words foxy landlady

explanation.surface: A plastic is kept on the premises by a cunning woman running a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Xylan is a hemicellulose, a natural polysaccharide found in plant cell walls, so it is a polymer.

clue.text: One sister went out, getting soaked

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a nun is a religious sister
went out, as with a romantic partner, means dated

explanation.surface: A sister goes out on the town and gets drenched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went out' means going out with someone, not leaving the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To be inundated is to be flooded or overwhelmed with water, so drenched or swamped.

clue.text: Where butter may be in a precarious situation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally resting on the blade of a knife
second meaning: the idiom for being in a finely balanced, risky position

explanation.walkthrough: Butter can literally sit on the blade before spreading; the idiom means poised between success and disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom pictures something balanced on a thin blade, ready to fall either way, hence tense and risky.

clue.text: Honouring Lennon, unwrapped jewellery

indicators.note: unwrapped means stripped of its outer layer, so Lennon loses its first and last letters

parts.note: bling is showy jewellery

explanation.surface: A tribute to John Lennon, the Beatle, with jewellery opened up.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to raise them to the peerage, a high honour, so the participle means honouring.

clue.text: They need to be paid for one held by mothers-to-be?

indicators.note: held by means kept inside, so one goes within the mothers-to-be

parts.note: pre-mums, people about to become mums
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Expectant mothers seem to be paying for a single item.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags PREMUMS as an invented word: mums before the birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance premiums are regular sums that policyholders must pay to keep cover.

clue.text: Metal lock controller?

parts.note: a lock of hair kept in place by a small metal clip, not a door lock

explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door or safe; here it is a lock of hair held in place.
explanation.definitionFit: This clip is a bent strip of metal that pins hair in place, keeping strands under control.

clue.text: Further statements offer justifications for suppressing unorthodox rites

indicators.note: suppressing means holding something down inside, so the rearranged rites go within reasons

parts.note: justifications are reasons

indicators.note: unorthodox means not in the usual form, so the letters of rites are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone defends outlandish ceremonies by holding them back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offer' and 'for' are link words joining the definition to the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A reassertion is a statement made again, so further statements repeating a claim are reassertions.

clue.text: Partial handicap I take for head of Latin

indicators.note: Partial says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A golfer reckons they will accept only part of their handicap.
explanation.walkthrough: Per capita is the Latin phrase meaning for each head.
explanation.definitionFit: In the phrase per capita, meaning per person, the Latin word for heads follows 'per'.

clue.text: Note charity book

parts.note: PS is a postscript, a note added to a letter
alms are charitable gifts to the poor

explanation.surface: A short note about a charitable book.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalms is a book of the Old Testament, a collection of sacred songs.

clue.text: Spaniard clutching another's drug

indicators.note: clutching means holding tightly, so one name is gripped inside the other

parts.note: Maria is a typical Spanish woman's name
another Spaniard is Juan, a typical Spanish man's name; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A Spanish person is caught holding someone else's narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spaniard' and 'another' each stand for a typical Spanish first name, one woman's and one man's.
explanation.definitionFit: Marijuana is cannabis, a psychoactive substance smoked recreationally.

clue.text: Indonesian script finally written

parts.note: Java is a programming language whose code is written as scripts

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of written

explanation.surface: An Indonesian writing system has at last been set down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'script' suggests an alphabet; it is the computer language Java.
explanation.definitionFit: Javan describes a person or thing from Java, the most populous island of Indonesia.

clue.text: Instruments found in the vicinity of muck?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the trumpets, trombones and horns section of a band

definitions.text: found in the vicinity of muck?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: money, from the Yorkshire saying where there's muck there's ...

explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'where there's muck there's brass' means dirty work pays; 'brass' is northern English slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both metal wind instruments and, as English slang, cash made from grubby trades.

clue.text: Right quartet in Peru, may be heading towards the source

indicators.note: in places the four inside the rearranged letters
may be suggests the letters of Peru and R could be put another way

parts.note: a quartet is four, the Roman numeral IV

explanation.surface: A group of four rightly travelling through Peru may be making for the source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quartet' is a number here, not a band of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upstream means travelling against the current, toward where a river begins.

clue.text: First half Martini (not quite), then half cocktail after a change of heart

indicators.note: half, with not quite as a nudge, keeps just under half of Martini, from its back end
change of heart means the middle letters swap round
half keeps the back part of cocktail

explanation.surface: A drinker takes a sip of a Martini, then half a cocktail, before changing their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half Martini (not quite)' gives INI, just under half. Half of 'cocktail' is TAIL; 'change of heart' swaps its middle letters to TIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An initial letter or stage comes at the very beginning, so the adjective means first.

clue.text: American reactionary before long is lying

indicators.note: before places the turned letters ahead of the next piece
reactionary means going backwards, so the letters of American's abbreviation are turned round

parts.note: to long is to pine

explanation.surface: A conservative American politician craving something is said to be dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' looks like telling untruths but means lying flat on the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying face upward, flat on one's back.

clue.text: Horse and sheep taken in as tools of my trade

indicators.note: taken in means held inside the word as

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A farm worker with a horse and a sheep regards them as the equipment of their job.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter speaks: rearranged letters are a crossword compiler's stock in trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Anagrams are a staple device in the setter's craft of building cryptic clues.
